en: Walking on wet fallen mango leaves is slippery because the smooth leaf surface reduces friction between your shoes and the ground.
The Moon's gravitational pull on Earth's oceans causes the regular rising and falling of sea water known as tides.
You can separate tiny pieces of magnetic iron ore called magnetite from black beach sand using a simple bar magnet.
Lightning is a massive spark of static electricity that jumps between clouds or from a cloud to the ground during thunderstorms.
Rainbows appear in the sky after rain because water droplets act like tiny prisms that bend and separate sunlight into colors.
You hear an echo in a large cave because sound waves bounce off the hard, flat rock walls and return to your ears.
Hot springs in Laguna are heated by geothermal energy, which is thermal energy transferred from hot magma deep inside the Earth.
Zigzag mountain roads like Kennon Road act as inclined planes to help vehicles climb steep slopes with less engine force.
Wind turbines in Burgos convert the kinetic energy of moving air from the monsoon winds into useful electrical energy.
The metal spoon in a bowl of hot sinigang soup becomes warm because heat conducts easily through the solid metal.
Your shadow is longest in the early morning because the low angle of the Sun blocks light across a greater distance.
Your body converts the chemical energy stored in rice into mechanical energy to power your muscles when you play outside.
